body: Will the feature be able to reset a task's progress and recalculate the hash to sign the breakdown?
This means a different skill content.  Right?  I don''t want the skill to be twice as long, because it has a condition in it for with-Lite and without-Lite.
Will the feature be able to reset a task's progress and mark-reviewed?
Any chance that MCP Apps (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/apps/overview) could fit this bill?

Mostly yes. The kernel (scripts, journal, hash lock) doesn't depend on the host, and Cursor 2.4+ reads .claude/skills and .claude/agents and has a blocking preToolUse hook. I added an 'Other hosts: Cursor' section with a gap table. The real losses: no skill-scoped hooks (they go in .cursor/hooks.json), a Stop hook that can't block, and it's undocumented whether preToolUse fires inside subagents. New question lite-cursor-host: my lean is Claude Code in v1, Cursor after a short spike on that last point.

I read this as 'NON-deterministic'. Agreed, and the draft only covered the scripts, not the model driving them. I expanded the warning and added three defenses that don't depend on the model being honest: per-attempt step tokens (a skipped step fails loudly), the final verdict printed verbatim from report.ps1 and never summarized, and a blocking Stop hook while the run is unfinished.
Thanks. I kept it as a design constraint, not a v1 requirement, so nothing Lite writes can rule it out later.

Yes to both, and they're now explicit. The subset table has rows for resume, reset (same safe/unsafe rewind rule as the harness, plus -y for a full rebuild) and review attestation. The kernel adds reset.ps1, mark-reviewed.ps1 and plan-hash.ps1, and there are acceptance items for each, including a plan-hash parity check against the binary. One heads-up: running sequentially on one branch means a scoped reset will more often REFUSE (a later non-descendant commit sits on top), and the message will say so.

Right, and your chosen option (one SKILL.md plus references/lite-profile.md) only works if we don't branch at every call site. There are about 60 (plan-breakdown 38, review 24), so that would double the skill. I added a note: each skill gets ONE preamble that maps 'guardrails <verb>' to '<verb>.ps1', and every Lite detail goes in the reference file, which loads only in the Lite profile. CI enforces a line budget (about 15 Lite lines per SKILL.md) and verb coverage. If you'd still prefer a physically separate Lite skill, say so and I'll reopen the question.

Good thought, but no on its own. MCP Apps is a UI surface (HTML in a sandboxed iframe) served by an MCP server, which is still a process on the machine (usually a Node package, so an npm dependency tree to review) or a remote service. That's the same security review, and the MCP Apps client list doesn't include Claude Code or Cursor. I added a 'Considered: MCP Apps' subsection and noted it on #824 as an optional run-status view for orgs that already approve an MCP server.
